plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win exactly when your value exceeds the second-highest bid (which is what you'd pay), and truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Since this is a single round with no repeated learning needed, and the format matches standard Vickrey auction rules, I will bid exactly my value of $33 to ensure optimal expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. This holds regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $15 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction, where bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since my value is $49 (the maximum possible), bidding my true value ensures I win whenever it's profitable to do so, and I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. There's no incentive to shade my bid since I don't control the price I pay upon winning—only the second-highest bidder's bid does. Thus, bidding $49 maximizes expected profit.
